newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs end higher, short-covering helps.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs end higher, short-covering helps.

text.p: Belgian bonds ended firmer and around session highs on Friday, pushed higher by short covering and with activity largely confined to professionals.
"The market's fairly volatile at the moment - it's a good hedge when it goes down," one dealer said. "There's been a bit of playing with the ten-year (OLO) today but no commercial flow."

The benchmark 2007 OLO was yielding 5.80 percent at the close versus 5.84 percent at the end previous session, its premium over Bunds remaining steady at seven basis points. June bond futures rose 10 basis points to 122.00.
Dealers noted a large buyer in five year paper.

Concerns about German and U.S. inflation, the prospect of a U.S. Federal Reserve FOMC policy meeting on July 1-2 and - to a lesser extent - Thursday's worrying comments from new French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on the state of the French budget deficit were all reasons for bond market caution, dealers said.
"Most people are sidelined. The drop in the Bund yesterday scared people and we're not going to see the 102 level (on the Bund future) soon," one added.
The markets had earlier shrugged off news of stronger than expected German M3 money supply growth data,
"The upward Bund trend remains in tact but we could go down before we go up again," the dealer said.
